# Ammonia synthesis (Haber-Bosch) (`ammonia_synthesis`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/chemistry.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Chemistry (`chemistry`)
- Deps: needs pneumatic_chemistry_gases, gas_laws; helped by refrigeration, coke_iron
- Core idea: Nitrogen from the air and purified hydrogen (historically obtained from water gas) combine to ammonia when pressed to about 200 atmospheres and passed over an iron catalyst at 400–500 °C. Only some 15 % reacts on each pass, so the ammonia is condensed out by cooling and the remaining gas is sent round again. Ammonia is turned into fertiliser salts or oxidised over platinum to nitric oxide, which is oxidised further and absorbed in water to make nitric acid. This removes the limit that manure, legumes and Chilean nitrate set on harvests, and also frees explosives from imported nitrate.
- Pitfalls:
  - Thinking the idea is the hard part. The reaction was known; the obstacle is large vessels and pumps for hot hydrogen at 200 atmospheres.
  - Hot hydrogen under pressure makes carbon steel brittle and bursts it; Bosch needed a soft-iron liner inside a vented steel shell.
  - Raising the temperature to speed it up lowers the yield; higher pressure favours ammonia at equilibrium. A catalyst speeds the approach to equilibrium without shifting it.
  - Traces of sulphur or carbon monoxide in the gas kill the catalyst.
  - It is not a pre-industrial project: it needs compressors, alloy steels, gas purification and instrument control.
- History: europe: 1774 Priestley isolates ammonia gas; 1898 Crookes warns of a coming nitrogen shortage; 1902 Ostwald's ammonia-to-nitric-acid process; 1909 Haber and Le Rossignol's laboratory apparatus (Karlsruhe); 1910 Mittasch's iron catalyst; 1913 Bosch's plant at Oppau (BASF); global: by the late 20th c. roughly half the nitrogen in human food comes from this process
- Read:
  - Vaclav Smil, Enriching the Earth: Fritz Haber, Carl Bosch, and the Transformation of World Food Production (2001)
  - Thomas Hager, The Alchemy of Air (2008)
